title: We're on a spectrum
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Where on the spectrum of risk do you live?

groups.heading: The risk is part of what makes it appealing

lines.text: I asked: what in our lives has created this entrepreneurial mindset, and what are we doing about establishing those habits, reading and absorbing information, and having a perspective of risk where you say: I am resilient to risk, take that risk away, I'm going to laser focus on the possibilities, not the impossibilities?

A student said: I think the risk is part of what makes it so appealing, because almost everybody on this call came from a high-friction childhood. A lack of pressure is almost worse than too much pressure. It's like a dopamine, adrenaline addiction. Make it chaos and I'll be the calmest person in the room.

We're on a spectrum, I said. Some of us are in an environment with the least chaos and the least risk. Others are in high-risk chaos. Some are in the middle, and other people are super high risk takers.

I told of people who are seventy years old and starting another business that will take ten years. I ask them: why? And they say: Jose, that's my nature. That's why I wake up every day. I'm not feeling alive unless I'm doing something this big.
Where on the spectrum are you, and are you happy there?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write where you sit on the spectrum: least chaos, middle, high risk.
Write what in your childhood put you there.
Write whether risk feels like an addiction or a choice.
Write one habit that helps you stay focused on possibilities.
Write what you would start at seventy, and why not start it now.

check.q: What did a student say a lack of pressure is?
choices: Almost worse than too much pressure

check.q: What image did I use for people's relationship with risk?
What did the seventy-year-olds say about starting a business?
choices: It's their nature; they don't feel alive unless they do something big

recap: Know where you are on the risk spectrum, and why.
